text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Communications ministry directs that five private telecommunications operators be connected to the network of state-run Nigerian Telecommunications Ltd which will enable subscribers of the two sets of operators reach one another.

- Two senior officials -- planning minister Ayo Ogunlade and Sam Aluko, chairman of the economic watchdog -- say to achieve economic growth Nigerians must invest in local enterprises instead of keeping scarce foreign exchange abroad.
- Oil minister Dan Etete, speaking at an oil conference in Lagos, urges banks and capital market operators to take advantage of deregulation by investing in the petroleum sector.

- Under the newly launched family economic advancement programme for which the government has set aside 4.3 billion naira, beneficiaries will get maximum of 550,000 naira loan for each project and will have to repay within three years.

- The price of resins produced locally for plastics industry has been increased by 11 percent to 80,000 naira per tonne but remains cheaper than the world price of $1,000 per tonne which excludes freight and insurance.

- United Nations Security Council has demanded an explanation from Nigeria over last week's visit to the country by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi in defiance of a U.N. embargo on flights from his country.
- Nigerian naira firms after government's declaration that it has no plan to devalue the local currency.
- Federal government is considering leasing public enterprises instead of privatising them, says industry minister Lieutenant-general Mohammed Haladu.
- Pfizer Products local management buys out technical partners shares and company now becomes wholly Nigerian-owned in a deal sealed at the Lagos stock exchange.
- Court strikes out suit by 67 bank executives seeking their release from detention. They are held under failed banks decree which sets stiff penalties for causing the collapse of banks.
- A 27-member Nigerian trade mission has arrived in New York to canvass for more United States investments in the country.
